description: Solo project exploring a researcher workflow to find comparable NASA microgravity combustion test runs, surface differences and missing values in material, geometry, oxygen, pressure, airflow and gravity, and produce source-linked summaries and reproducible evidence briefs. Intended as a research aid, not certified safety advice.
summary: Fire Evidence Explorer is a research workbench for NASA’s Flame in Freefall challenge. It brings 31 NASA FLEX microgravity combustion tests into one place so researchers and students can find comparable runs, inspect the recorded conditions, and trace each finding to the exact source cell. The Visual Evidence Lab shows how measurements vary across runs, while Comparison Context separates test conditions from outcomes and flags missing measurements. Users can save guided investigations, export evidence briefs, and ask an optional DeepSeek assistant for explanations grounded in the selected runs. The result is a reviewable way to explore what the experiments support and where the evidence is limited.
details:
Fire Evidence Explorer addresses Flame in Freefall by making NASA FLEX experimental records easier to find, compare, and verify.

Open the workbench at https://fire-evidence-explorer.vercel.app/. Source code is publicly available at https://github.com/desanv01/fire-evidence-explorer-spaceapps-2026.

The workbench ranks candidate runs by agreement in recorded conditions. Select two or three runs to compare measurements in their original units, then open a citation to see the original CSV row, column, and value. FLEX-004 burned 3.34 seconds longer than FLEX-001 under different recorded conditions. That difference describes the selected runs and does not establish a cause. Unreported measurements remain unknown.

The Visual Evidence Lab plots native measurements and counts omitted runs. Comparison Context separates test conditions from outcomes and keeps the complete gas composition visible. Investigation Notebook includes three guided investigations and supports explicit local saving, JSON import/export, and a printable report.

The app uses TypeScript, Next.js, React, and Zod. It runs on Vercel. DeepSeek Flash provides optional cited explanations and bounded assistant action proposals, with a shared attempt limit enforced through Upstash Redis. The evidence tools and recorded examples remain available without a live model call.

AI disclosure: Codex and DeepSeek Harness assisted with development, debugging, technical writing, design, and verification. DeepSeek Flash generated optional evidence explanations and the labeled recorded example. FLEX measurements come from NASA, and plots and comparison values are computed from those records. The demo uses authentic app images, a HyperFrames composition adapted from my MajuPilot video design, and Microsoft Zira synthetic English narration. The video has a visible disclosure.
